 This Petition, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

The petitioners are before this Court calling in question registration of a crime in Crime No.28/2023, pending before the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and CJM, D.K.District, Mangaluru,
for the offences under Sections 420, 465, 467, 468, 471 and 120B of the IPC.

2. Heard Sri Nishit Kumar Shetty, learned counsel for petitioners, Sri P. Thejesh, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 and Sri S. Rajashekar, learned NC:
2024:KHC:27328 counsel for respondent No.2. The matter is moved today for reporting settlement.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioners and learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that the parties to the lis have settled the dispute among themselves before the civil Court in O.S.No.195/2023 and have filed an application under Sections 482 r/w. 320(2) of the Cr.P.C.
seeking permission to compound the afore-quoted offences along with the affidavits of the respective parties.

4. The affidavit of the complainant, reads as under:
"AFFIDAVIT 3.

It is submitted that apart from the aforesaid proceedings, several cases and counter cases have been filed by the parties and the same were pending before the jurisdictional Courts and now all the dispute between the parties are settled amicably on the intervention and mediation of the family members, relatives, friends and well-wishers.

It is submitted that in view of the amicable settlement arrived by the parties, the detailed Compromise Petition is filed in O.S. No.195/2023 pending on the file of the II Additional Civil Judge at Mangaluru wherein both the parties have also agreed to report settlement in Criminal Petition pending before this Hon'ble Court and recording the said Compromise, O.S. No.195/2023 came to be disposed of Veena K Rai vs State Of Karnataka on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24725008/

sentences.text: 3 in terms of the Compromise Petition by an order dated 27.03.2023.
In view of the compromise arrived between the parties, NC: 2024:KHC:27328 respondent no.2 has no objection to quash the entire proceeding against the petitioners for the aforesaid offences.

4. It is submitted that offence under Section 420 of IPC is compoundable with the permission of the court and offence under section 465, 467, 468, 471, 120(b) of I.P.C.
are non-compoundable in nature but in view of facts and circumstance of the case since the petitioners and the 2nd respondent have amicably settled the matter between themselves, the 2nd respondent has for quashing the entire proceedings against the Petitioners.

In view of the facts and circumstances of the case, it is just and proper to permit the parties to compound the offence alleged against the Petitioners and quash the entire proceedings in P.CR. NO.08/2023, subsequently the FIR in Crime No.28/2023 registered by the Kavoor Police Station against the petitioners for the offence punishable under sections 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, 120(b)
of I.P.C., on the file of I Addl. Senior Civil Judge and CJM, D.K. District., Mangalore,
Otherwise the Petitioners will be put to irreparable injury and hardship

Wherefore, it is prayed that this Hon'ble Court be pleased to permit the parties to compound the offences against the Petitioners and quash the entire proceedings against the petitioners in P.CR. NO.08/2023, subsequently the FIR in Crime No.28/2023 registered by the Kavoor Police Station against the petitioners for the offence punishable under sections 420, 465, 467, 468, 471, 120(b) of I.P.C., on the file of I Addl. Senior Civil Judge and CIM, D.K District., Mangalore, in the interest of justice."

5. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER a. The criminal petition is disposed.
b. The impugned proceedings in Crime No.28/2023, pending before the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and CJM, D.K.District, Mangaluru, stands quashed.
